title: Opal Dream
full_review:
"Opal Dream" (Strand) shines like the gemstone in its title.

Set in an Australian outback mining colony, the gently charming tale revolves around Kellyanne (Sapphire Boyce), an 8-year-old with a vivid imagination who becomes heartsick over the disappearance of her two make-believe friends, Pobby and Dingan, after her concerned father, Rex (Vince Colosimo), "takes them" to work with him for the day, hoping that his daughter will be motivated to play with real children for a change.

When Rex returns late at night without her imaginary mates, a distraught Kellyanne implores her dad to drive back up to the mine to look for them, triggering unintended consequences that cause the locals to turn against him and his wife, Annie (Jacqueline McKenzie), until the supportive efforts of their 11-year-old son, Ashmol (Christian Byers) -- worried about his sister's deteriorating emotional and physical condition -- win over the town.

Director Peter Cattaneo's adaptation of the Ben Rice novel "Pobby and Dingan" celebrates themes of family, community and the value of childlike faith in a way that's genuinely sweet while avoiding excess sentimentality, with tender performances by Boyce and Byers.

Given the story's rough-and-tumble milieu, there's a light sprinkling of salty language and, in one scene, Rex gets beaten by angry miners who accuse him of trespassing on their claims, but overall this is a family-friendly, lovely little film.

The film contains brief violence, some crude expressions and a fleeting instance of profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-II -- adults and adolescents. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG -- parental guidance suggested. Some material may not be suitable for children.
